name: portfolio
title: Portfolio
description: A plain gallery wall for your own work: your name and what you do set large, a grid of pieces grouped into series, then an optional CV (Experience, Education), commissions with prices, and a big email address to reach you.

images.purpose: the signature piece, full width under your name; without it the name and line stand alone
images.alt_hint: what the piece shows, e.g. A cyanotype of fern leaves on blue paper
images.prompt: the person's own best piece, cropped wide; never generated

images.purpose: one piece of work per card in the work grid (6-60, 1600 px on the long edge; shown 4:3, the first one large); a card without a picture shows its name set large on a tinted plate
images.alt_hint: what is in the piece, not 'photo', e.g. Poster: a red heron over a grey harbour
images.prompt: the person's own work, photographed or exported flat; never generated

images.purpose: a small round mark beside your name in the masthead (32 px) and the browser icon
images.alt_hint: e.g. The initials I C in a circle
images.prompt: a simple monogram of the person's initials, flat, in the palette's accent colour on white

images.purpose: the lead picture on a project's own page
images.prompt: the project's lead piece, from the person's own work

images.purpose: more pictures inside a project page: put ![description](image) on its own line
images.prompt: further pieces or details from the same project, from the person's own work

images.purpose: the picture when a link is shared; empty uses the hero

content.purpose: the big line at the top: your name and what you do, e.g. Ines Calder draws maps and book covers
a sentence or two under it
the work grid's heading when cards have no group; with groups each group is its own block under its group name
sorts cards into blocks, in card sort order: series of work (e.g. Selected work, Posters), commissions, and for a CV: Experience, Education
CV mode: a card with a period (e.g. 2021 – now) prints as a CV line: period, then name (the role or degree), subtitle (the employer or school) and description
a card with a price (and no period) prints as a commission or service: name, price, description, link
on a work card: a small line like the medium and year; on a CV line: the employer or school
on a work card, makes the whole piece a link, usually to its project page in a stream
list streams print as dated lists (projects, exhibitions, news); entries with an event split into upcoming and earlier. A feature stream shows its newest entry in full
the About block; its first paragraph is set large
the Contact block: the email set large, phone, address, and social links
small buttons under the contact details, e.g. Download CV (PDF), with a note
one line across the top, e.g. your availability: Booking commissions for spring
the menu; empty uses the home sections and Contact
the footer line, e.g. your name and a copyright

art.ask: Ask for the person's best 6-12 pieces and which one leads. The work stays theirs; the assistant never generates samples of it.
art.style: The person's own work, shown on a plain page; nothing competes with it. The palette is neutral (Ink, Slate) so colours in the work read true; Midnight suits photography. Use real photos for real things; never make up pictures of real places, people or food. Illustrated art only for a mark or emblem, in the palette's accent colour.
steps: Collect the pieces from the person, with which one leads (it becomes the hero, and the first card shows large).
Check each: at least 1600 px on the long edge, sharp, sRGB, nothing cropped that matters. Don't recompress below the site's own resizing.
Agree the order and the groups (series, commissions, Experience, Education) with the person; set each card's sort.
Write alt text for each piece: what is in it, not 'photo' or 'image'.
Use real photos for real things; never make up pictures of real places, people or food. Illustrated art only for a mark or emblem, in the palette's accent colour.
Upload each one (an https link in its field, or photo_upload_link), then call theme_needs: every slot should say filled.
